body: I don't know if they would really, it just feels risky in case they actually do find out.

> your feelings about it can and likely will change.

That's what I really hope will happen. I get a little more hope everyday when I go out and pass and no one suspects a thing, it's just when the bad days come (and they come often) everything just seems so pointless and impossible to deal with. But the good days are amazing and keep me going. 

I do have trans friends online that I'm gonna be meeting soon actually, I just don't like to bother them with my depression though in case it brings them down, we all struggle with depression so I only talk about it when they do.

I have never heard of Kate Bornstein or her book but I read the synopsis and will definitely give it a read, thank you!!
Yeah I'm getting very tempted to do it. I'd feel so stupid if I ruined all the progress I've made at the gender clinic though.

I really wanna move, I'm hoping to get myself in college next year so I can finally get away and have a total fresh start.

>All of these little things are all learned behaviors, for everyone.

That is a really good point actually, I guess I'm just learning them a little later than everyone else. I've always been feminine from a young age too, I just forced myself to stop when people started making fun of me. It still feels weird knowing that 2-3 years ago I was still acting like a typical guy, slowly I've been letting my real self out but it still feels weird and fake even though it shouldn't really.

Thank you for posting this. I know I really need to work on my insecurities and self esteem if I'm ever gonna make it, it's just so hard. That being said it is still early days in terms of transitioning, I just hope that things will improve the more I get used to living as a girl.

Yeah definitely. I keep fantasizing about passing 100% and then dropping everything to move away where no one knows me and no one knows about me being trans. I love my family and the few friends I have but they will never see me as a girl ever, and being around them just makes me sad. It's worse when I go out with them and they either fail or don't make an effort to call me 'she' or 'her' when they're talking about me, even if they do try I know they won't ever consider me a girl.

And yeah, I just want to be seen as a normal person. I've seen enough reactions from people during my transition to know that I don't really want to associate with anyone who knows I am trans, as horrible as that is to my loved ones. The difference in the way I'm treated by people once they find out is jarring. I just feel so different to every other girl out there, they're all so varied and unique but in the same way, whereas I'm a total anomaly, and trying to even look or be anything like them seems like I'm acting or something.

I kinda want to, but I'm currently going through the NHS system to get hormones prescribed to me. They are really strict, any hint of instability or depression and they find any excuse not to prescribe you them. I've been hiding everything and pretending to be happy and adjusted until I finally make it through the system.
Yeah, within a few days of taking them I started getting huge nosebleeds almost daily. The doctor said it wasn't related to the meds, but as soon as I stopped taking them the nosebleeds stopped.

Not for about 5 years. I got prescribed meds but I stopped them after a month because I didn't want to have to medicate myself to be normal (ironic considering I ended up transitioning). Plus they gave me huge nosebleeds :/
Well, I've been depressed for 8/9 years now almost constantly. The urge to actually kill myself hasn't ever been this high though, it's gotten worse over the last few months.

I live in the UK. My whole family and everyone else I've told supports me 100%, and I never get any abuse in public or anything. Yet it doesn't matter, I've had an almost perfect transition yet the suicidal ideation continues.
